The recurring trigger

An estimate changes when its inputs do.

A single total can conceal a classification assumption, an old tariff date, or an unassessed charge. Show the components and the uncertainty before comparing scenarios.

Required inputs

  • Quantity, unit price, and valuation assumptions
  • Provisional classification, origin, and scenario date
  • Duty assumptions and cost components

Prepared output

  • Included-components subtotal for each scenario
  • Excluded costs and unvalidated inputs
  • Simulated change explanation and review task

A specific review sequence

Make each step inspectable.

01

State the assumptions

Keep the unvalidated customs-value input and invented duty rate visible.

02

Compare included components

Recalculate goods and duty as inputs change; show fixed fees separately.

03

Reopen affected reviews

A changed fixture creates a review task, not an automatic approved update.

01 / Inside the proposed module

Follow each component into the subtotal.

The HX-42 fixture separates goods, illustrative duty, freight, insurance, and broker fee. Freight here is a cost line, not a legal valuation conclusion.

Inspect the synthetic example

02 / Inside the proposed module

A tariff change is a review trigger.

A dated simulated change appears beside the original assumption. It does not overwrite a reviewed dossier or promise production monitoring.

Inspect the synthetic example

03 / Inside the proposed module

Keep the old calculation in the history.

An input edit creates a proposed scenario revision. Review remains separate, and a lower estimate never determines the classification.

Inspect the synthetic example

Controls & scope

What the output
can—and cannot—settle.

Invented rates are not tied to actual HTS codes. MPF/HMF where applicable, additional tariffs, AD/CVD, taxes, and valuation adjustments are unassessed. No guaranteed duty quote or savings.

Expected reviewer: importer compliance owner and customs broker; counsel where the question requires it.

Review the limits

The pilot question

Would this help the
broker prepare the entry?

Whether source-dated scenarios help the broker locate assumptions; valuation questions, calculation rework, and reviewed change handling.

Discuss offer 4

Before the next step

Questions for this offer.

A clear boundary is part of a useful review.

All questions
Are these actual tariff rates?

No. The demo uses invented 4% and 6% rates to explain arithmetic, without assigned HTS codes.

Is the $240 difference a saving?

No. It is the difference between two conditional, incomplete scenarios. A classification cannot be selected by whichever costs less.
